clue.text: Modest just the same

definitions.meaning: a modest person is natural and free of airs or pretension
remaining just the same means being left unchanged by something

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a lack of pretension and being unchanged or untouched by an influence.

clue.text: State university raises capital investment

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: a hat is something one invests (clothes) the capital, or head, with

explanation.surface: A state university puts up money for a capital investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raises' turns HAT upwards to give TAH. 'Capital' is the head, and to invest once meant to clothe, so headwear is the capital investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Decoding any signal that's broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is scattered far and wide, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Somebody deciphers whatever signal is being transmitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the nine letters of ANY SIGNAL; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoding a message means analysing it closely to work out what it says.

clue.text: Decline to meet a composer

parts.note: to decline is to drop or fall

explanation.surface: Someone refuses an introduction to a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' reads as refusing, but it means a drop; Manuel de Falla was a Spanish composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuel de Falla was a twentieth-century Spanish composer, so the name is an example of a composer.

clue.text: Gains favour with hot dishes

definitions.meaning: from the idiom to curry favour with someone, ingratiating oneself
spicy dishes of Indian origin cooked in a sauce

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'curry favour' supplies the first sense, and spicy Indian stews the second.

clue.text: Paper-train

definitions.meaning: the Daily ... is a British national newspaper
a fast train making few stops

explanation.definitionFit: The Daily Express is a British newspaper, and an express is a fast train with few stops.

clue.text: It makes a pass into a path

definitions.text: It makes a pass into a path

parts.words: It makes a pass into a path
parts.note: a speech defect that sounds an S as TH would turn the word pass into the word path

explanation.definitionFit: A speech impediment in which the S sound comes out as TH, exactly turning one word into the other.

clue.text: I owned a small property in this state

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I had, and had means owned
HO is the abbreviation for house, a modest property

explanation.surface: A homeowner tells of a little place they had in this state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I owned' is I HAD, shortened to I'D; HO is the abbreviation for house; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state of the USA, pointed to as the state referred to.

clue.text: Urge a chap to become a PR man

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them
a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: Someone encourages a fellow to go into public relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A press agent is employed to handle publicity, which is the work of a public relations man.

clue.text: Bully one who works around a colliery

indicators.note: the worker's letters go around the colliery, enclosing it

parts.note: a doer is someone who acts or works
a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A miner is intimidated by a fellow pit worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the container; 'a' is a link, and 'Bully' is a verb here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to bully, ruling over others in an overbearing way.

clue.text: A number grow sick, get benefit

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: Many people fall ill and claim sickness benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: V is five in Roman numerals, a stock way for 'number' to give a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail oneself of something is to make use of it and gain from it, getting benefit.

clue.text: Concerning a will he's shameless

parts.note: re means about or concerning
probate is the legal proving of a will, standing here for the will itself

explanation.surface: A man in a dispute over an inheritance is said to have no shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he's' is a link; RE is the stock crossword word for 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprobate as an adjective means unprincipled and without shame.

clue.text: Many diet perhaps, but this could end in a big blow-out

definitions.text: this could end in a big blow-out

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the phrase might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Lots of people go on diets, though dieting may end in a huge binge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges MANY DIET; 'but' is a link. The definition puns on a blow-out as a feast and as an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive charge ends in a blast, which is a blow-out in the explosive sense.

clue.text: One studies images

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to con is an old word meaning to study or learn

explanation.surface: A single person pores over pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: To con is to study, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Icons are images, particularly religious pictures or representative symbols.

clue.text: A miller surely likes a rest from it!

definitions.text: A miller surely likes a rest from it!

parts.words: A miller surely likes a rest from it!
parts.note: the everyday tedious routine, taken literally as a miller's corn-grinding every day

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a tedious everyday routine, and a miller literally grinds every day.

clue.text: Gets off with a slight dislocation

indicators.note: a dislocation puts things out of place, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone escapes with only a minor dislocated joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dislocation' rearranges A SLIGHT; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to get off a vehicle, such as a bus or train.

clue.text: They stockpile hard roes for cooking

indicators.note: food prepared for cooking is changed, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: People store away fish roe until it is cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' rearranges HARD ROES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarders are people who amass and store up supplies, stockpiling them.

clue.text: Trying to interview royalty?

parts.note: to see someone can mean to meet or interview them
a king is a member of royalty

explanation.surface: A reporter attempts to get an audience with a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeking to do something is trying to do it, an attempt.

clue.text: Engaged in current affairs?

parts.note: involved in what is going on, read literally as being out in the water's current

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fully involved in what is happening, and literally describes a swimmer in a current.

clue.text: Many tease girl about being a slowcoach

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, so a large number
to rag someone is to tease them
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Lots of people make fun of a girl for being slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses DRAGGAL; 'being a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A laggard is someone who falls behind, a slowcoach.

clue.text: Acts in a degrading way

parts.note: reads as behaving shamefully, but means reducing someone in rank

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who demotes others lowers their rank or grade, literally de-grading them.

clue.text: Strait-laced girl enters into the joke

indicators.note: the girl's name goes inside the joke

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A prim girl joins in with the fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters into' puts RITA in PUN; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Puritan, in the general sense, is a person of strict, prudish morals.

clue.text: Sack and what may be put in it

definitions.meaning: to sack a town is to loot it

definitions.text: what may be put in it
definitions.meaning: loot, the stolen goods that might be stuffed into a sack

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to loot, and as a noun the loot that a sack might hold.

clue.text: Lofty but not upright

definitions.meaning: a ... piano lies horizontal, unlike an upright piano

explanation.definitionFit: Grand means imposing, and a grand piano is the horizontal kind rather than the upright.

clue.text: He'd follow the account with a pained expression

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man looks pained after reading his bank statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follow' signals the order in the down clue. The definition is loose: one who ached would likely wear a pained expression.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ached is to have felt pain, the state a pained expression shows.

clue.text: They form some unit of Canadian police

indicators.note: to form is to shape, so the letters are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A squad describes itself as part of Canada's police force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' rearranges SOME UNIT; 'They' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police are informally called Mounties.

clue.text: Go to bed, having lost direction in Italy

indicators.note: having lost means one letter is taken out

parts.note: to turn in is to go to bed
N stands for north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A traveller retires for the night, lost somewhere in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost' removes N (north) from TURN IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy, capital of Piedmont.

clue.text: Find love on the German river

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Someone finds romance on a German river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts O above DER; 'Find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river of central Europe forming part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: From being in the red I possibly came into money

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone in debt suddenly comes into a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IN THE RED I; 'From being' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have inherited is to have received money or property from someone who died, coming into money.

clue.text: Pulled together, perhaps, but fell out

definitions.meaning: oarsmen pulling together on the oars, as one example
to fall out is to quarrel or argue

explanation.definitionFit: Spelt the same, it means used oars and also, said with a different vowel, quarrelled.

clue.text: They're assumed to be failures

definitions.meaning: clothes are assumed, or put on; slang for clothes
a dud is something that fails to work

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for clothes, which one assumes or puts on, and for things that fail.

clue.text: Moon-starer extraordinary

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters fall out of order

explanation.surface: Someone who gazes at the moon remarkably well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges MOON-STARER; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who studies the moon and stars scientifically is literally an exceptional moon-starer.
